root.name: Scandinavian Defense: Boehnke Gambit
root.moves: 1. e4 d5 2. exd5 e5 3. dxe6 Bxe6

overview: Black plays 2...e5 instead of recapturing the pawn, giving a second pawn after 3.dxe6 Bxe6 to get quick development and open lines. White is a pawn up and plays Nf3, d4 and Bd3 or Be2 to consolidate. Black hopes for activity with ...Nc6, ...Qd7 and ...O-O-O, but the compensation is considered lacking.

white_ideas.idea: Nf3, d4 and Bd3 to develop and consolidate the extra pawn.
Return the pawn only when it brings a clear edge.

black_ideas.idea: Develop fast with ...Nc6, ...Qd7 and castle long.
Pressure on the open e-file and d4.

typical_structures.structure: Open position with White's extra pawn and Black's rapid piece play.

character.notes: Black sacrifices for open lines and attacks; White can lose track.

gambit.notes: White is a pawn up and can hold it with simple development.

soundness.notes: Considered unsound by strong players; Black's compensation is thin.

structure.notes: Open centre; the e- and d-files open.

approach.notes: Strong players seldom use it; surprise value.

level.notes: Trap-based, dubious, so not a beginner choice.

character.reason: Black plays for rapid development against a pawn up.

gambit.reason: Black gives a pawn that White can keep.

soundness.reason: Strong players think Black lacks enough compensation.

structure.reason: Open lines and files straight away.

level.reason: Dubious, so never beginner; traps and lines to memorise.

plans.reason: Black gives a pawn for time and piece activity.
